newsitem.title: GREECE: Albanian army retreats after clash with rebels.
newsitem.headline: Albanian army retreats after clash with rebels.

text.p: The Albanian army retreated after a clash with armed insurgents which left four villagers and at least two soldiers wounded in southern Albania on Wednesday, reporters and other eyewitnesses said.

"Eyewitnesses just told us that the battle is over and the troops withdrew," Dimitris Stefos, an ex-prefect in the southern port of Sarande, told Reuters by telephone. "The fighting lasted about 40 minutes and at least two soldiers were wounded."
Hospital officials in Sarande said they were treating four people for gunshot wounds received during the battle near the village of Styari, 10 km (six miles) east of Sarande.
A Greek Skai television reporter on the scene also said the locals had won the battle. The soldiers got in trucks and drove towards the town of Delvine, several km (miles) to the east, he said.
"The people won. The army, about 60 soldiers, got into their trucks and drove away," Stefos said.
